sections.text:
On a very hot summer day, when the sun was burning the earth and not a single drop of rain had fallen for many weeks, there was a black crow feeling an intense thirst that was about to kill him.

The crow looked for any water spring or small pond to drink from, but all the streams and ponds had dried up completely due to the intense heat.

The crow almost lost hope, and its flight became very weak, to the point that it thought of surrendering to death from extreme thirst and exhaustion.

Suddenly, the crow spotted a large pottery jar (jug) placed in the shadow of an old wall.

The crow flew towards the jar with all his remaining strength, and eagerly landed on its edge, hoping to find some water.

The crow looked inside the jar, and was very happy when he saw that there was actually some pure water at the bottom of it!
The crow tried to put its beak in to drink, but the pitcher was deep, and the water level was very low at the bottom.

The crow's neck was not long enough to reach the water, and he tried repeatedly to stretch his neck as far as he could, but to no avail.

The crow tried to turn the heavy jar so that the water would pour out of it so that he could drink it from the ground, but the jar was very heavy and made of thick pottery, and he could not move it an inch.

The crow felt desperate again. Water was in front of him, but he could not drink it! Will he die of thirst with water just steps away from him?
But the crow was not a stupid bird, but rather it was intelligent and thoughtful.

He stopped making random attempts and sat aside thinking about a solution to this difficult problem.

The crow looked around the place, and noticed many pebbles and small stones scattered on the ground near the wall.

A genius idea flashed into the crow's head! He flew towards the ground and picked up a small pebble with his beak.

The crow returned to the jar and dropped the pebble inside.

“Knock.”

The pebble fell to the bottom, and the water level rose very slightly.

The crow was happy with this result, so he flew and picked up a second pebble, and dropped it into the jar, and the water rose even more.

Then he picked up a third, fourth, and fifth pebble, and continued this hard and tiring work despite his intense thirst.

The crow was flying back and forth, collecting pebbles and dropping them into the jar one by one, and each time he dropped a pebble, the water would rise slightly to the top because of the volume occupied by the stones at the bottom.

After the crow dropped dozens of pebbles, the water finally rose until it reached the edge of the jar, within reach of its beak!
The crow drank the cool, refreshing water until he was completely quenched, and his strength, activity, and life returned to him thanks to his sound thinking and not giving up.

The crow folded its wings and flew high into the sky, pleased with the success of its plan.

Thus, this story teaches us that necessity is the mother of invention, and that intelligence, calm thinking, and the insistence on trying can solve the most complex problems, no matter how impossible they seem at first.
